annotation.title_clean: House Bill 751 / Senate Bill 676 - An Act relative to vehicles operated by unconventional means (platooning)
annotation.title_en: House Bill 751 / Senate Bill 676 - An Act relative to vehicles operated by unconventional means (platooning)
annotation.summary_en: Tennessee bill (HB 751/SB 676) authorizing vehicle platoons, groups of vehicles traveling at electronically coordinated speeds, on state roads after notifying transportation and safety departments, with a 30-day non-rejection rule. It adjusts registration, following-distance and operator definitions, and requires CDL drivers in commercial platoon vehicles.
key_provisions_or_claims: Defines 'platoon' as vehicles traveling in a unified manner at electronically coordinated speeds
Operators must notify TDOT and Department of Safety with a platoon operations plan; deemed approved after 30 days absent rejection
Commercial vehicles in a platoon must have an endorsed CDL driver behind the wheel
Registration certificate may be carried only in the lead vehicle
Operator of a platoon is the person controlling the lead vehicle
